newsitem.title: USA: Acordia agrees to be acquired by Anthem.
newsitem.headline: Acordia agrees to be acquired by Anthem.

text.p: Acordia Inc said it signed a definitive merger agreement with Anthem Inc, under which Anthem would acquire all the outstanding stock of Acordia for $40 a share.
The agreement was approved unanimously by a special committee of Acordia's outside directors. Anthem currently owns 66.8 percent of Acordia's outstanding common stock.

"We believe the tender offer price is fair and that the proposed transaction is in the best interests of Acordia and its stockholders," John Crane, chairman of Acordia's special committee, said in a statement. "We look forward to an orderly completion of this transaction."

As proposed, Anthem and a wholly owned subsidiary will make a tender offer, which is expected to begin no later than June 6, for all the outstanding shares of Acordia's common stock that Anthem does not already own.

The deal is subject to several conditions, including the tender of at least a majority of the Acordia shares owned by parties other than Anthem. After the tender, remaining Acordia shares would be acquired in a cash merger for $40 a share.
The merger plan follows an announcement in February that Acordia and Anthem were initiating strategic reviews of their business and strategic relationship.

Anthem also said that its previously announced discussions with a third party regarding the sale of Acordia's brokerage business are continuing. However, the tender offer and proposed merger are not conditioned upon the sale of the brokerage business.
Acordia provides insurance broking and consulting services through a nationwide network of companies. It is the fifth largest insurance brokerage firm in the United States and the world.
Anthem is a Fortune 500 mutual insurance company, providing health care management and health insurance products and services.
